subject: Post-call: evaluation goals, model recommendations & plan for observed regressions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varela <elena.varela@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: evaluation goals, model recommendations & plan for observed regressions

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment for the eval: 

- Goal: measure model fit for Nimbus chat assistant (product lookup + returns handling) across: accuracy of slot extraction, hallucination rate on policy questions, and latency under peak traffic (p95).
- Initial recommended controlled models to evaluate (we'll run the same promptset you shared):
  • redwood/longform-rl2: best quality baseline (higher cost, higher context handling)
  • open/qlora-13b-8k: strong token efficiency for short queries
  • redwood/ggml-v1.4-8bit: cost-optimized candidate (we recommend pinning for production after pass)

I've attached the prompt set you used (nimbus_promptset_v1.txt) and our lightweight benchmark summary (benchmarks_nimbus_20260620.pdf). Next steps I propose:
  1) We run a 48-hour evaluation across those 3 model variants with your promptset and the sample traffic distribution you supplied.
  2) We surface per-prompt accuracy metrics + token cost breakdown and share a short diff report if any model version changes introduce regressions.
  3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up on Monday 6/29 to review results and decide pin/rollback.

Please confirm you want us to kick off the eval. If you already have any explicit SLOs (e.g., max hallucination < 2% for policy Qs), send them over and we'll include pass/fail thresholds.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

---
Attachment: nimbus_promptset_v1.txt (text)
Attachment: benchmarks_nimbus_20260620.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Varela <elena.varela@nimbusretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khanna <samir@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation goals, model recommendations & plan for observed regressions

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear plan. Please proceed with the 48-hour eval. A few notes from our side: 

- SLOs: hallucination on policy questions <= 1.5%; slot extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the sample set.
- One urgent note: after your team upgraded the hosted default model yesterday (our production /fast endpoint got the v20260624 runtime), our CS team flagged a spike in incorrect policy answers in the live logs. I've attached a short diff with three representative examples (diff_examples_nimbus.txt).

Can you confirm whether the eval run will be isolated from the current production variant? If the regression is tied to the new runtime, we may need an emergency rollback to the previous pinned version while you run the eval.

Elena
Head of Product — Nimbus Retail
elena.varela@nimbusretail.com

---
Attachment: diff_examples_nimbus.txt (text)

Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call: evaluation goals, model recommendations & plan for observed regressions

Folks — forwarding the thread. Customer reports live-quality regressions after our hosted default model update (v20260624). They included 3 short examples.

Requested actions:
- Quick triage from infra/serving side to check if a model variant rollout or kernel change touched their endpoint.
- If it's a clear regression, propose immediate rollback to the prior runtime (v20260610) for their tenant and run the 48-hour controlled eval on a pinned variant until we confirm quality.
- Ben/Marissa: can you prepare an exec summary + estimated downtime/risk for a rollback? I want to propose a rollback window (1 hour) and a canary ramp if possible.

Elena: we will prioritize this. Monica — can you own the customer comms and confirm rollback authorization?

Thanks — Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Elena Varela <elena.varela@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 06:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call: evaluation goals, model recommendations & plan for observed regressions

Jordan / team / Elena — quick technical readout from infra/serving perspective: 

- Initial find: the v20260624 rollout included a kernel patch that changes default temperature handling for short-context policy prompts. This can increase paraphrase variance on policy Qs in some few-shot prompt shapes.
- Repro: I replayed the three diff_examples against both runtimes (v20260610 and v20260624) using the provided promptset. Results: 2/3 examples show a clear change in output where v20260624 produced policy-contradictory phrasing. I've uploaded the raw diff output to the shared drive link in the thread.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Pin Nimbus tenant to the previous runtime: runtime:v20260610 (safe rollback) — target rollback start: Sat 27 Jun 2026 09:00 PDT. Expected impact: sub-5-minute switch for the tenant if we trigger their dedicated config rollback; we will do a canary (5% traffic) for 10 minutes, then 20%, then full cutover.
2) Run the 48-hour eval on a non-prod pinned variant: redwood/ggml-v1.4-8bit (cost-optimized) + redwood/longform-rl2 (quality baseline). We'll include the specific promptset and the diff examples so the eval captures this regression.
3) If rollback is approved, enable a short-term SLA credit (we'll propose 1 week of waived Dedicated overage for the regression window) as a goodwill gesture once we confirm the root cause.

Technical notes for the ops run: rollback steps are documented here: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/rollbacks/runtime-rollback (internal). Please let infra know ASAP so they can schedule the change.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: raw_repro_output_v20260624_vs_v20260610.txt (uploaded to shared drive)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varela <elena.varela@nimbusretail.com>, Samir Khanna <samir@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call: evaluation goals, model recommendations & plan for observed regressions

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Ben — and Monica, thanks for being on standby.

Elena: proposing the following customer-facing plan (please confirm authorization):

1) Immediate: schedule rollback to runtime:v20260610 at 09:00 PDT today with a 30-minute canary window (1 -> 5 -> 25 -> 100% over approx 30m). This should revert the behavior you saw in production.
2) Short-term: run the 48-hour evaluation on pinned variants (redwood/ggml-v1.4-8bit and redwood/longform-rl2) using your promptset and the three diff examples; share a structured diff report within 48 hours of run completion.
3) Follow-up: 30-min sync Mon 6/29 10:00 PDT to review results and agree the pinned production model or additional mitigations.
4) Goodwill: we'll apply a one-week credit for dedicated overage during the regression window once we confirm root cause.

If you authorize the rollback, reply with a single-line approval and I'll trigger the infra run. We'll copy you the rollback timeline and the canary traffic logs.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
